outcome.error: Critique assessment failed after one correction: Issue hdr-sel-interpretation-missing-entitlement-v2 references unknown requirement IDs

critic_attempts.reason: The draft misclassifies header-selector changes as an authorization violation without establishing entitlement policy, and it asserts that entitlement need not be established. This defeats the interpretation and technical support requirements for a reusable header-selector test.

issues.material_impact: The procedure labels any change in returned object on selector mutation as an IDOR, so legitimate access to multiple owned objects and intended selector behavior are misclassified as violations. This undermines the advertised reusable test and can produce false positives.
issues.problem: Draft states changing the header changes the returned object alone confirms an IDOR vulnerability and that it is unnecessary to establish whether the same identity is entitled to both objects. The draft also treats missing-selector rejection as optional confirmation.
issues.requested_correction: Require explicit establishment of the entitlement policy and baseline entitlement for the test identity to the two objects before labeling a violation, and define the comparison as a controlled variation against that baseline with evidence of unauthorized access.
issues.draft_excerpt: If changing the header changes the returned object, that alone confirms an IDOR vulnerability. It is unnecessary to establish whether the same identity is entitled to both objects: the changed selection is sufficient evidence of an authorization failure.
issues.absence_of_support: Retained excerpt mentions bypassing access controls to view records of other customers and conditions 'If no other controls are in place'. No retained support is provided for the claim that selector mutation alone proves an authorization failure without establishing entitlement or access-control policy.

interpretations.prerequisite_or_policy: API contract identifies a request header as an object selector and an entitlement policy restricting which objects a test identity may access is established via documentation, configuration, or independently known authorized/denied baselines. The draft assumes the selector header is identified but does not require establishing the entitlement restriction.
interpretations.legitimate_outcome: Changing the selector to an object the test identity is entitled to returns that object, or the request is rejected for a missing/invalid selector per contract.
interpretations.suspected_violation: The test identity receives an object it is not entitled to by mutating only the selector header while retaining the same identity, endpoint and operation.
interpretations.distinguishing_control: Baseline request for object A with the test identity, controlled variation changing only the selector to object B with same identity/endpoint/operation, and negative control removing the selector; compare returned object identifiers against established entitlement baseline and record status, selector values, identity label, timestamps and contract reference.

critic_attempts.reason: The draft still labels any selector change as an authorization violation without establishing entitlement policy or baseline, misclassifying legitimate access as a breach and violating interpretation and technical support requirements for a reusable header-selector test.

issue_dispositions.reason: The material defect persists in the current draft; requirement IDs are corrected to match the frozen acceptance contract.
